plainTranslation: A's love and values meets B's dreams. The opposition pulls them into push-and-pull.
policy: Governed by synastry-policy. Descriptive, not deterministic; intensity is never treated as obligation, safety concerns override astrology.
note: Synced from authored synastry bundle synastry-authored__19_ (2).json.
summaryDeep:
This person may feel just out of reach, even when they are close.

There is often a strong pull here. You may feel drawn to their beauty, mystery, kindness, imagination, or the feeling they awaken in you. The relationship may seem meaningful before it has had time to become clear. You may feel that something important is happening, even if you cannot name what it is.

At its best, this aspect gives both people something they need. One brings love into the room in a real way, through affection, presence, and attention. The other brings a sense of wonder, meaning, and possibility. Together, love can feel both human and larger than human.

But the opposition can keep you reaching.

One person may want the dream to become concrete. The other may want ordinary affection to become something endless, spiritual, or ideal. Both may be drawn to a version of the relationship that exists partly in the space between what is known and what is imagined.

That space can be intoxicating. It can also be confusing.

This is where the fog can go both ways. You may believe the other person is offering more than they have actually offered. They may believe you understood something they never clearly said. One person may become evasive because they do not want to disappoint. The other may become self-protective because the uncertainty starts to hurt. Before long, both people are responding to the story around the relationship, not the relationship itself.

In its shadow, Neptune can show up as unavailability, broken promises, vague intentions, not responding, avoidance, lying, or gaslighting. That does not mean this aspect predicts those behaviors. It means that when the bond begins with bliss and then becomes unclear, you have to name what is happening instead of explaining it away as romance.

Come back to what is actually happening between you. Not the story you have built around them. Not the future version of the relationship you hope will arrive. The person in front of you.

Longing can be powerful, but it is not the same thing as intimacy. The relationships that endure are not sustained by fantasy alone. They are built through the choices two people make to show up.
